answer.exemplar: A media query is answered by the environment the document is being presented in, and the environment knows a viewport, a resolution, a colour scheme, and a pointer type, but it has no way to ask about one particular element or box, so a condition such as min-width: 600px is asking how wide the area the page is being laid out in is. Every element on the page gets the same answer, which is what makes a query useful for deciding the page's shape and also what makes it easy to misread: a developer who writes max-width: 700px expecting it to mean that one narrow component is 700 pixels wide has actually written a rule that switches the whole page whenever the window is narrow, and a component that genuinely must respond to its own width needs the feature that answers that question, a container query, which is evaluated against the element's container instead of the viewport.

questions.explanation: A model answer must say what the condition is answered by, that every element gets the same answer, and give the mistake that follows from expecting an element's own width.
questions.hint: Ask what the condition is allowed to know about the page.
questions.learningObjective: explain what a media condition is evaluated against and the mistake that follows

answer.exemplar: A preprocessor runs before the browser ever sees the sheet: it reads the file, replaces every use of its variable with the text it was given, and passes on the finished sheet, so the browser receives no variable at all and the substituted text cannot change afterwards. A custom property is a different kind of thing, declared in the sheet, inherited like any other property, and resolved at each element from that element's own declaration or an inherited one, so it can differ from place to place and can be changed by a script while the page is running. That is what lets one custom property carry a value through a whole subtree and be re-pointed at the root to restyle everything below it, and it is also why a custom property cannot go everywhere a preprocessor variable can: a media query's condition has to be known before any element is involved, so a value that only exists on an element cannot be used there.

questions.explanation: A model answer must place the preprocessor before the browser ever sees the sheet, place the custom property's resolution at each element while the page runs, and give one place where only the preprocessor can work.
questions.hint: Ask when each one is replaced with a value, and what the browser receives.

questions.explanation: A fractional track is a share of a leftover, so the leftover has to be found before the share can be. The container's content width is the starting figure; the gaps and any track given a definite size are removed from it, because neither is available to the fractional tracks; what remains is divided by the sum of the fr weights to give the value of one fr; and each track is then that value times its own weight. The order matters because step two changes the number step three divides, which is why a 20 pixel gap in a 500 pixel container is worth 20 pixels of every fractional track rather than being divided among them.
questions.hint: Ask what has to be known before a share of what is left can be computed.

options.misconception: believes the space is divided by the number of tracks, not the weights
options.text: Divide what is left by the total weight of the fr tracks
